name: assertthat
resume: CRAN assertthat 0.2.1 is pure R. All 26 exports are translated. has_extension calls tools file_ext. Failure messages come from the same expressions R deparses.

functions.name: %has_args%
functions.done: Calls has_args without exact. This wrapper does not carry has_args's failure handler, so a miss uses the default deparse.

check.case: mean %has_args% "x" and mean %has_args% "y"

functions.name: %has_attr%
functions.done: The same function as has_attr. The infix is parsed as a call to that function.

check.case: 10 %has_attr% "a" and has_attr(has_attr, "fail")

proof.python:
import statistics
import time

def show(res):
    if res is True or getattr(res, "value", None) is True:
        return "TRUE\n"
    if isinstance(res, str):
        return res + "\n"
    return res.msg + "\n"

def one():
    from assertthat import has_attr, see_if
    z = 10
    return show(see_if('z %has_attr% "a"')) + show(has_attr(has_attr, "fail"))

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(value, end="")
print("MS")
print(f"{statistics.median(elapsed):.17g}")

functions.name: on_failure<-
functions.done: Sets the failure handler. Python calls set_on_failure because it has no replacement functions.

check.case: is_odd(2) before the handler, then after on_failure<-

proof.python:
import statistics
import time

def show(res):
    if res is True or getattr(res, "value", None) is True:
        return "TRUE\n"
    if isinstance(res, str):
        return res + "\n"
    return res.msg + "\n"

def one():
    from assertthat import assert_that, is_number, see_if, set_on_failure
    from assertthat.expr import render
    def is_odd(x):
        assert_that(is_number(x))
        return x % 2 == 1
    before = show(see_if("is_odd(2)", env={"is_odd": is_odd}))
    def fail(call, env):
        return render(call["x"]) + " is even"
    set_on_failure(is_odd, fail)
    after = show(see_if("is_odd(2)", env={"is_odd": is_odd}))
    return before + after

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(value, end="")
print("MS")
print(f"{statistics.median(elapsed):.17g}")

functions.name: assert_that
functions.done: Returns true when every expression is true, and raises assertError with the failure message otherwise.

check.case: is.numeric(1), 5 < 4, and a long isTRUE() call past the 60-character deparse cutoff

proof.python:
import statistics
import time

def show(res):
    if res is True or getattr(res, "value", None) is True:
        return "TRUE\n"
    if isinstance(res, str):
        return res + "\n"
    return res.msg + "\n"

def one():
    from assertthat import AssertThatError, assert_that
    def message(expr):
        try:
            assert_that(expr)
        except AssertThatError as error:
            return error.args[0]
        return "NOERROR"
    ok = "TRUE" if assert_that("is.numeric(1)") else "FALSE"
    short = message("5 < 4")
    long = message("isTRUE(10 + sqrt(25) + sum(1:10) + sqrt(25) + sum(11:20) + sqrt(25) + sum(21:30) + sqrt(25) + sum(31:40) + sqrt(25) + sum(41:50))")
    return ok + "\n" + short + "\n" + long + "\n"

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(value, end="")
print("MS")
print(f"{statistics.median(elapsed):.17g}")

functions.name: see_if
functions.done: Evaluates each expression and returns true, or false with the failure message. An assertError inside an assertion becomes that message.

check.case: character, length, scalar, string, directory, custom message, equality, and any()

proof.r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(assertthat))

show <- function(res) {
  if (isTRUE(res)) "TRUE\n" else if (is.character(res)) paste0(res, "\n") else paste0(attr(res, "msg"), "\n")
}
one <- function() {
  x <- 1
  out <- character()
  out <- c(out, show(see_if(is.character(x))))
  out <- c(out, show(see_if(length(x) == 3)))
  out <- c(out, show(see_if(is.scalar("a"))))
  out <- c(out, show(see_if(is.string(1:3))))
  out <- c(out, show(see_if(is.dir(17))))

  out <- c(out, show(see_if(are_equal(x, 1.999, tol = 0.01))))
  out <- c(out, show(see_if(any(c(FALSE, FALSE)))))
  out <- c(out, show(see_if(5 != 5)))
  paste0(out, collapse = "")
}

import statistics
import time

def show(res):
    if res is True or getattr(res, "value", None) is True:
        return "TRUE\n"
    if isinstance(res, str):
        return res + "\n"
    return res.msg + "\n"

def one():
    from assertthat import see_if
    parts = []
    x = 1
    parts.append(show(see_if("is.character(x)")))
    parts.append(show(see_if("length(x) == 3")))
    parts.append(show(see_if('is.scalar("a")')))
    parts.append(show(see_if("is.string(1:3)")))
    parts.append(show(see_if("is.dir(17)")))
    parts.append(show(see_if('is.dir("asdf")')))
    parts.append(show(see_if("5 < 3", msg="Five is not smaller than three")))
    parts.append(show(see_if("noNA(c(TRUE, NA))")))
    x = 2
    parts.append(show(see_if("are_equal(x, 1.9)")))
    parts.append(show(see_if("are_equal(x, 1.999, tol = 0.01)")))
    parts.append(show(see_if("any(c(FALSE, FALSE))")))
    parts.append(show(see_if("5 != 5")))
    return "".join(parts)

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
